## Showcasing an agentic AI concierge at LEAP 2026

Sourced fact: Horizontal Digital is co-exhibiting with Salesforce at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh from August 31 to September 3, unveiling a Digital Concierge demonstration built on Salesforce Agentforce and focused on travel, tourism, and hospitality use cases [1].

Sourced fact: The demonstration is designed to show how an agentic AI experience can guide guests from their first inquiry through booking and on-site service in real time, illustrating an end-to-end interaction pattern within defined hospitality scenarios [1].

Limitation: The companies are presenting a demo rather than announcing a commercial rollout, and the public materials do not enumerate detailed operational or transactional functions beyond guiding the guest journey through inquiry, booking, and on-site phases; the scope and boundaries of the orchestration shown at LEAP are not specified in greater technical depth [1].

Sourced fact: George Smith, Managing Director EMEA at Horizontal Digital, and Matthew Lambert, Regional Alliances & Channels Director, Middle East at Salesforce, are identified in connection with the initiative, which the companies say supports Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 digital modernization goals in experience-led sectors [1].

## From siloed tools to integrated experience ecosystems

Sourced fact: The announcement emphasizes a broader shift in Saudi Arabia’s digital landscape from isolated point solutions toward integrated experience ecosystems that combine data, artificial intelligence, and composable technologies, with the Digital Concierge positioned as a concrete illustration of this direction [1][2].

Analysis: In the context of hospitality, an integrated experience ecosystem means aligning guest-facing touchpoints (such as discovery and booking) with operational systems and partner services under a unified data and governance model, so that an AI agent can reason over the same, consistent customer and inventory context throughout a stay; this continuity reduces context handoffs and enables the agent to maintain state across stages of the guest journey while operating within enterprise policies.

Analysis: An agentic workflow on a platform like Salesforce Agentforce benefits from cohesive data models and orchestration layers in which prompts, tools, and policies are grounded in first-party records; in practical terms, this allows the AI to select and sequence appropriate tools—such as search, availability queries, or itinerary assembly—based on intent and constraints surfaced from trusted data, while keeping actions auditable and bounded by role-based controls and business rules.

Limitation: The LEAP 2026 materials do not detail the Digital Concierge’s reference architecture, including which data sources are unified, what orchestration techniques are employed, or how guardrails are implemented for safety and compliance; specifics such as connectors, data residency approaches, and governance mechanisms are not described in the announcement [1].

## Composability for travel and real estate in Saudi Arabia

Sourced fact: Beyond hospitality, the companies frame the initiative within a strategy to modernize digital ecosystems for travel and real estate in Saudi Arabia, aligning with a move toward composable, data-driven experiences tailored to large-scale developments and experience-centric operations [1][2].

Analysis: Composable technologies—modular services exposed via APIs and packaged business capabilities—allow operators to assemble guest experiences and property-service flows as interchangeable building blocks; this supports rapid iteration across diverse venues and developments by swapping or extending components (for example, search, reservation logic, or post-stay engagement) without replatforming entire stacks.

Analysis: In high-growth environments such as Saudi giga-projects, composability enables consistent patterns for onboarding new properties and partners into a unified journey map; standardized interfaces and policy templates help ensure that each new brand or venue can plug into shared identity, catalog, availability, and service orchestration layers while preserving its unique content, offers, and operational nuances.

Analysis: Data integration is foundational to this approach, typically involving canonical models for guest, property, and inventory entities; identity resolution across web, app, contact center, and in-venue interactions; and consent and preference management that can be enforced uniformly across channels—capabilities that allow an agentic AI to reference reliable, authorized context at every turn of the guest journey without duplicating or fragmenting records.

Limitation: Neither the announcement nor the related strategy perspective provides performance benchmarks, deployment timelines, or named pilot customers for the Digital Concierge; there are no disclosed metrics on accuracy, latency, or containment rates, and no public roadmap for productionizing the demo’s patterns across multiple brands or properties [1][2].

## Execution path under Vision 2030

Sourced fact: Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 program prioritizes digital modernization across key sectors, with tourism and hospitality designated as central pillars of economic diversification; the Digital Concierge initiative is presented as directly supportive of this agenda by demonstrating integrated, AI-driven experiences purpose-built for regional needs [1][2].

Analysis: A guided, end-to-end guest journey aligns with Vision 2030 by showcasing how unified data and AI can streamline trip discovery, booking confirmations, and on-site interactions, offering consistent service quality across rapidly expanding destinations; such demonstrations help establish reference patterns for orchestrating experiences at the scale and complexity required by multi-operator, multi-property developments.

Analysis: Positioning the demo on Agentforce highlights a platform-centric approach to governance, auditability, and extensibility that can be critical for national-scale programs; standardizing on composable, policy-aware building blocks allows public and private stakeholders to replicate best-practice journeys across different operators and regions while maintaining localized controls, language support, and integration with domestic infrastructure.

Limitation: While the demo illustrates the promise of agentic experiences, the announcement does not specify localization details such as multilingual experiences, regional hosting options, or integration with Saudi regulatory frameworks for data protection and sovereignty; clarity on these dimensions would be necessary to assess readiness for broad deployment within the Kingdom [1].

Question: Which source systems and data domains are included in the Digital Concierge demo’s unified context (for example, property management, availability, loyalty, or service case records), and how is data residency handled for Saudi deployments?

Question: What governance and safety mechanisms—such as tool-use policies, human oversight checkpoints, and audit logs—are implemented within Agentforce for this hospitality scenario, and how are they tuned for regulated environments?

Question: How will the teams measure success beyond the demo, including experience quality, response accuracy, and time-to-resolution across inquiry, booking, and on-site phases, and what timeline and partners (if any) are targeted for pilot implementations in Saudi Arabia?
